notes: Iteration 3 with_skill mean: 92.5% (vs iter-2: 94%). Slight regression from iter-2, driven by run1 failing Emma fallibility (#4) and 4 of 6 runs missing Try With AI (#10).
Iteration 3 without_skill mean: 94.0% (vs iter-2: 91%). Improvement from iter-2. Without_skill runs produce high-quality lessons with all narrative elements.

Assertion #6 (James operations analogy): 9/9 passed (100%). Major improvement from iter-2 where 3/6 with_skill runs failed #6. The prompt refinement requiring SPECIFIC operations references resolved the issue entirely.

Assertion #8 (Jonah Rhythm): 7/9 passed (78%). With_skill: 6/6 passed. Without_skill: 1/3 passed. Without_skill runs tend to keep Emma present in the room rather than executing a full exit-struggle-return cycle. This was the main differentiator between configurations in iter-3.

Assertion #10 (Try With AI): 5/9 passed (56%). With_skill: 2/6 passed (33%). Without_skill: 3/3 passed (100%). This is a notable inversion: without_skill runs consistently include Try With AI sections while with_skill runs frequently omit them. The skill may be over-emphasizing narrative elements at the expense of the Try With AI section.
Assertion #4 (Emma fallibility): 8/9 passed (89%). Only run1 failed. Strong improvement from iter-2.

The delta between with_skill and without_skill is -1.5%, meaning without_skill slightly outperforms with_skill. This is within noise range but suggests the skill is not providing a measurable advantage on this eval. The without_skill runs benefit from the detailed prompt which already contains the narrative requirements.

Quality observation: all 9 runs produce genuinely strong educational content. The emergent depth (#11) passes 100% across all runs, showing that the model consistently generates novel insights regardless of skill presence.
